events.title: CVE-2026-109445 (CVSS 9.8): PLANET GS-5220-8P2T2S V3 Stack-Based Buffer Overflow Fixed
events.summary: PLANET Technology has patched two vulnerabilities in its GS-5220-8P2T2S switch, including a stack-based buffer overflow tracked as CVE-2026-109445, in firmware v3.2412b261022. The record urges users to update their switches; the headline cites a CVSS score of 9.8 for the buffer overflow, though the structured data does not confirm that score.
events.why_it_matters: A maximum-severity buffer overflow in a network switch could allow remote compromise of the device, so any organisation running this model should treat patching as urgent. The record states the fix is available now, but does not report exploitation in the wild, KEV listing, or EPSS data for this flaw. The related CVEs mentioned (CVE-2026-12591 and CVE-2026-20320) concern different products and are not part of this switch advisory.

claims.text: CISA lists CVE-2026-20320 as exploited in the wild, added 2026-11-10, with US federal agencies due to fix it by 2026-11-24.
CVE-2026-12591 is rated 9.9 (critical) under CVSS 3.1 by the CNA that assigned it, the highest of the 4 scored CVEs here.
FIRST's EPSS puts the chance of CVE-2026-12591 being exploited in the next 30 days at 1.7%, the highest of the 3 CVEs here.

events.title: Cybersecurity’s Next Test Is Better Decisions, Not More Alerts

events.why_it_matters: It signals to security leaders that buying more tools or collecting more telemetry can widen the gap between spending and effective response. Defenders may need to prioritise decision-making workflows, evidence gathering across disconnected systems, and governance rather than additional alert volume.

events.title: A little something extra comes preinstalled.
events.summary: Bitdefender researchers describe a campaign called Midnight Mimosa in which low-cost Android devices ship with malware already installed, so phones are compromised before first use. The malware runs with system-level privileges, enabling silent app installation and removal, ad and click fraud, device information collection, and use of infected phones as residential proxy nodes for botnets.
events.why_it_matters: Preinstalled compromise means device hygiene steps like factory resets will not remove the malware, so buyers of low-cost Android hardware inherit infection by default. System-level privileges allow the phones to be quietly repurposed for fraud and as proxy infrastructure feeding larger botnets. Organisations should treat cheap consumer Android hardware as a potential trusted-channel risk.

events.title: Apache APISIX 3.20.0: Seven Fixes to Check Before Upgrading

events.why_it_matters: Organisations running APISIX as their API gateway should check whether their plugin setups fall within the affected conditions before upgrading. The record notes no CVEs, severity rating, or evidence of exploitation, so risk assessment rests on the release itself.

events.why_it_matters: Driver's licence numbers are high-value identity data that can support fraud and identity theft, so affected drivers may face lasting risk. The incident also illustrates how sensitive personal data held by vendors can expose a company's workforce even when the company itself is not breached.
